description_full: Zoom Communications, Inc. provides an Artificial Intelligence-first open work platform for human connection in the Americas, the Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The company offers Zoom Meetings that offers HD video, voice, chat, and content sharing through mobile devices, desktops, laptops, telephones, and conference room systems; Zoom Phone, a cloud phone system; and Zoom Team Chat enables users to share messages, images, files, and content in desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile devices. It also provides Zoom Docs, a modular workspace; Zoom Whiteboard, an interactive canvas; Zoom Clips for capturing video and screen content; Zoom Rooms, a software-based conference room system; and Workspace Reservation. In addition, the company offers Zoom Contact Center, an omnichannel solution; Zoom Revenue Accelerator, a conversation intelligence software for Zoom Meetings and Zoom Phone; Zoom Events to manage, host, market, and report on all of virtual and hybrid events; Zoom Webinars Plus; and Zoom Webinars which supports interactive video presentations to large audiences. Further, it provides Workvivo, an all-in-one employee experience platform; Zoom Developer Platform and App Marketplace which integrates platform with other applications, platforms, websites, and services; and Zoom Apps. It serves individuals; and education, entertainment/media, enterprise infrastructure, finance, government, healthcare, manufacturing, non-profit/not for profit and social impact, retail/consumer products, and software/Internet industries. The company was formerly known as Zoom Video Communications, Inc. and changed its name to Zoom Communications, Inc. in November 2024. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: Zoom Communications, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $26.2B market cap on $4.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +3.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 56% against a 11% cost of capital — a 45-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 76% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.9B in free cash flow — roughly 40 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.05× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 6.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 16% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 23% operating margin runs 16pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.99x).
It accounts for 0.1% of sector revenue and 0.1% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-7.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 15% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 12% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 22% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 45% and a beta of 1.23, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $245.1M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 29% in the 2020 crash and 65% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 30% below its DCF fair value of $128, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 36%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $96.86 to $179 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 8.3 vs 26.7 and P/FCF 13.6 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 64% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.3% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 26 covering analysts target $119 on average, 32% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 56% clears the cost of capital of 10.9% by 45pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.19).
It runs a 76% gross margin and converts 40% of revenue into free cash flow, or 24% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.05x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.2x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 7pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 17.4% of revenue on R&D and 15.6% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $7.8B (5% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 9.4, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.5% over 3 years and 12.9% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 117%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 6.7% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.08 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 86% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 5%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (1.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 79%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (40 sales, net $11.7M sold).
It returns 6.2% a year to shareholders (6.2% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 1.1% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 7,438 employees, each generates about $655K of revenue, 1.8x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 40.9% a year.
That works out to $259K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $817K (1x revenue per employee).
